classification.difficultyReason: Model equal distances with linked speed and time changes, eliminate a variable through a reciprocal relationship, then solve and interpret the resulting quadratic.

content.prompt:
A train travelled 240 km at a certain speed. When the engine was replaced by an improved model, the speed increased by 20 km/hr and the travel time decreased by 1 hr.
What was the speed of each engine?

answer.short: Original speed: $60\text{ km/h}$; new speed: $80\text{ km/h}$. Use $240=st$ and $240=(s+20)(t-1)$.
answer.worked:
Let the original speed be $s$ km/h and the original travel time be $t$ hours. Using $d=st$:
$$\begin{align*}
240&=st\\
240&=(s+20)(t-1)
\end{align*}$$
Substitute $t=\dfrac{240}{s}$ into the second equation:
$$\begin{align*}
240&=(s+20)\left(\frac{240}{s}-1\right)\\
240s&=(s+20)(240-s)\\
240s&=220s+4800-s^2\\
s^2+20s-4800&=0\\
(s+80)(s-60)&=0\\
s&=-80\text{ or }60
\end{align*}$$
Since speed is positive, $s=60$. The original speed is $60\text{ km/h}$ and the new speed is $60+20=80\text{ km/h}$.
Check: $240\div60=4$ hours and $240\div80=3$ hours, a decrease of $1$ hour.
